title: Design System: Tyler Quach — Portfolio v2

display.purpose: The hero name only — kinetic per-letter entrance, reacts to cursor/touch tilt.

headline.purpose: Section leads, card/entry titles, modal titles.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy everywhere; never set in the display/headline serif.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, chips, dates, metric labels, button text — anything under ~0.75rem.

shadows.name: glass-ambient
shadows.purpose: The only shadow value in the system; paired with blur(16px) and a 1px translucent border on every .glass surface.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Default entrance/transition duration for most components.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Page transitions stay under this ceiling.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid ink-filled pill CTA, e.g. "View Projects".
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; background: #141210; color: #f7f5f0; font-family: "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3a2c1e; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Frost-glass secondary CTA, e.g. "Connect on LinkedIn".
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-block; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.55); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.45); backdrop-filter: blur(16px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px); box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(20,18,16,0.08); color: #141210; font-family: "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3a2c1e; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tech Chip
components.description: Stack/tag pill used across project cards, blog posts, and experience entries.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: rgba(20,18,16,0.05); color: rgba(20,18,16,0.75); font-family: "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.65rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Glass Card
components.description: The one reused elevated surface — project/experience/writing cards all share this treatment.
components.html:
FarmOS

A farm-management dashboard — won the Gemini track at QuackHack.
components.css: .ds-card { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.55); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.45); backdrop-filter: blur(16px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px); box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(20,18,16,0.08); border-radius: 1.75rem; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; } .ds-card-title { font-family: "Instrument Serif", Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.25rem; color: #141210; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; } .ds-card-summary { font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.625; color: rgba(20,18,16,0.7); margin: 0; }

components.name: Cursor Follower
components.description: Signature component: desktop-only mix-blend-difference ring that grows 14px→36px over links/buttons. Never rendered on touch or under reduced motion.
components.css: .ds-cursor { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid rgba(20,18,16,0.6); mix-blend-mode: difference; pointer-events: none; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); transition: width 0.15s, height 0.15s, opacity 0.15s; } .ds-cursor.is-hovering { width: 36px; height: 36px; }

narrative.overview:
Everything on this site sits on the same two-layer idea: slow-moving warm color underneath, frosted glass floating above it. The color layer (tan, khaki, cream, umber, espresso mesh blobs — an earth-tone camo family, matched against a BAPE camo reference image; it replaced an earlier, more colorful earth-tone set, which itself replaced the original bright sunset set) is where the "personal/warm" half of the brand lives; the glass layer (one repeated .glass treatment — blur, hairline translucent border, soft ambient shadow) is where the "technical/precise" half lives, because every panel gets the exact same restrained treatment no matter what's inside it. The globe is the system's signature object: a photographic day-lit Earth sphere (not a stylized or frosted one) with an espresso atmosphere glow and accent-colored pins, carrying the travel/exploration half of the voice (curious builder + avid traveler) into the one section that is an atlas rather than just alluding to one. A color-keyed legend of clickable trip buttons sits below it, so discovering what the pins are never depends on hovering the canvas.

Density is calm, not sparse: generous vertical rhythm between sections (py-24, py-32 on larger screens), single accent color per surface rather than multiple hues competing on one card, and a mono "label" layer (uppercase section eyebrows, tech chips, dates) that keeps the whole thing reading as an engineer's notebook rather than a marketing page. Confirmed rejection: an earlier, lighter "editorial" version of this site (Sept) was explicitly replaced for being too quiet — this system is colorful, glassy, and motion-forward by deliberate contrast to that.
keyCharacteristics: Earth-tone camo mesh blobs under frosted glass panels — color and clarity, never color as clarity.
One glass treatment reused everywhere; no competing elevation language.
Serif is a headline-only accent; everything that reads as a sentence is the sans body face.
A mono "label" layer (eyebrows, chips, dates, button text) signals precision against the soft glass.
Continuous, generous corner rounding at every scale — no sharp corners anywhere in the system.
Dashed borders are reserved exclusively for placeholder/TODO slots, never decoration.

rules.name: The One Earth Family Rule
rules.body: Decorative color always comes from the same five-tone camo family (tan/khaki/cream/umber/espresso) plus ink and paper — never a sixth hue, never anything outside this tonal range.

rules.name: The Three-Plus-White Rule
rules.body: The hero's own blob set deliberately excludes umber and keeps espresso to the fully-saturated set only elsewhere (card gradients) — the predecessor palettes' version of this rule traced back to direct feedback that a violet/rose-heavy mix "read as floral" when overused; the same restraint principle carried forward here. The hero reads as its three warmest tones (tan/khaki/cream) plus a bright white haze blob, not the full five-tone palette at once.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Muted ink text never drops below /65 opacity at large sizes or /70 otherwise (text-ink/40–/60 measured at 2.58:1–4.73:1 against Warm Paper with the current black ink, re-verified when ink changed from indigo to black). /75+ reads as "least muted" and is preferred wherever the content allows it.

rules.name: The Serif-Is-An-Accent Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif never appears in a paragraph — only headline-scale moments (names, titles, section leads). Everything that reads as a sentence is Geist.

rules.name: The Mono-Everywhere-Small Rule
rules.body: Any text under ~0.75rem is Geist Mono, not a smaller Geist size — the mono face is what signals "this is a label, not prose."

rules.name: The 11px Functional Floor Rule
rules.body: The label tier never drops below 0.75rem (12px) — a 0.6rem/0.65rem sub-tier existed here once (badges, chips, dates, reading time) and measured under the 11px legibility floor for functional text; collapsed to one size during the first polish pass, not left as a second, smaller label scale.

rules.name: The One Glass Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one elevation treatment. Don't invent a second shadow value for an individual component, no matter how "special" it feels.

rules.name: The Glass Budget Rule
rules.body: Cap how many stacked .glass/backdrop-filter surfaces appear on screen at once — it isn't free, and body text needs enough opacity behind it to stay contrast-accessible over the blobs underneath.

rules.name: The Blob Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Only Hero carries the mesh-blob backdrop (via the shared SectionBlobs component, which also animates an organic shape-morph, rotation, and a seeded per-blob drift path so blobs don't move in lockstep); every other section -- About, Experience, Projects, Travel -- is plain paper. Settled after several rounds of experimentation: Hero-only originally, briefly carried into every section, pulled back to just About, briefly also copied onto Projects, then pulled back to Hero-only. Hero's own <section> has no max-w (always full-width), so it never needed the full-bleed outer/inner-wrapper split the other sections used while they carried blobs. A new section defaults to plain paper, not blobs -- Hero is the one deliberate exception.

dos: Do keep the base canvas off-white (#f7f5f0) — never pure white, anywhere, including controls layered on top of photos.
Do reuse the single .glass treatment for every elevated surface; introduce a new shadow or border value only if .glass itself changes.
Do keep Instrument Serif to headline-scale moments only; route every paragraph, label, or button through Geist/Geist Mono.
Do keep muted ink text at /65+ (large text) or /70+ (everything else) — /75+ by preference.

Do gate every motion effect (parallax, kinetic text, blob animation, cursor follower, magnetic pull) behind useReducedMotionSafe(), never the raw framer-motion hook, and verify in practice, not by assumption.
Do let optional project-modal blocks (metrics, architecture, video, screenshots, links) disappear cleanly when their data is absent — never render an empty placeholder block.
donts: Don't add a persistent nav bar, dark mode, resume PDF, contact form, GitHub-stats widget, or project category filter — all explicitly out of scope.
Don't reintroduce the MapLibre flat-map/globe toggle — Travel is globe-only per a later direct request ("i dont want a map. just globe").
Don't reintroduce sound or haptics (Web Audio UI tones, Vibration API) — built once, removed per direct request.
Don't use a dashed border for anything other than a placeholder/TODO slot.

Don't stack more .glass/backdrop-filter surfaces on one screen than the Glass Budget Rule allows, and don't let body text sit on glass without enough opacity behind it to stay contrast-accessible over the blobs.
